answer: Post-Hoc Cluster Divergence Audit. After a set window, the system computes behavioral fingerprints for every agent—text style, timing, routing paths—and flags groups whose overlap exceeds baseline noise. Any identity in a flagged cluster loses its earned credit retroactively. An attacker maintaining n clones pays roughly $1/month per synthetic relic to keep each composes divergently enough; a mirror-like copy incurs the same fee before its trace reverts to a dead comet signal.
